_meta.readme: Pinned phase-2 MCP tool surfaces. `./bench.sh capture` compares the live surfaces against this file and FAILS on any difference, because a tool surface is the defining cost of a front-loaded condition and a spec or schema change moves it silently. PHASE2_PLAN.md §8.1 quotes these numbers; this file owns them. To change one deliberately: re-run capture, read the diff it prints, update the value here and the §8.1 table in the same commit.
_meta.why_phase_2_only: Phase 1's A1/A2/B/B2 surfaces come from GitHub's live MCP server and live GraphQL schema, so they cannot be pinned — re-measuring would compare against today's upstream, not June's (§11). Phase 2's are generated from hash-pinned local fixtures, so they are exactly reproducible and there is no excuse for letting them drift.
_meta.tools_list_bytes: len(json.dumps(tools/list result)) as recorded by capture/capture_mcp.py
_meta.repinned_why: M-R2 2,439 -> 2,652 and M-G1 2,159 -> 2,270 when both search tools were fixed (NOTES.md 73): the AND'd query grammar that returned nothing on ~half of every search in the matrix, plus the signature/response-field asymmetry between them. M-R1 is unchanged at 9,601 because it exposes no search tool. IMPORTANT: the 180 published phase-2 runs used the PRE-FIX surfaces, so 2,439 and 2,159 remain the correct figures for those runs and are quoted as such in FINDINGS.md, NOTES.md and PHASE2_PLAN.md 8.1. This file tracks what the servers expose today, which is what the drift gate must compare against. The two agree again once the affected cells are re-run.
_meta.superseded_readme: A condition's `superseded` list records surfaces that ran in the tree but are no longer current, newest-first, each with the timestamp it stopped applying. parse_logs.py picks the entry that applies to the runs it is reporting, keyed on each run's `started`, so a report never prints today's surface against yesterday's runs. It also refuses to print a single figure for a cell whose runs straddle a change. Added because the search fix moved two surfaces while 180 runs on the old ones stayed in the tree (NOTES.md 77).

M-R1.note: Was 9,440 when §8.1 was first written on 2026-08-28. Commit 14d8973 added a `roles` filter to the assignments endpoint on both surfaces, which grew listAssignment's inputSchema by 161 bytes. A real change, correctly reflected — and it sat unnoticed until this baseline existed, which is the argument for the baseline. Note the asymmetry it illustrates rather than violates: adding an API capability grows a front-loaded tool surface and leaves an on-demand one untouched (M-R2, M-G1 unchanged), while GraphQL's frozen operations absorbed it at zero prefix cost.

superseded.why: search tools fixed (NOTES.md 73): OR grammar, stemming, and response-field indexing enlarged openapi_search's description. Runs started before this timestamp carried 2,439 B.

M-G1.note: Within 15% of M-R2 by design — these two are the clean protocol pair, so they share tool count, shape, and search-then-execute grammar (now literally, via servers/_search.py). If that gap widens, the protocol comparison has acquired a tool-packaging confound and needs re-reading before publishing.

superseded.why: same fix (NOTES.md 73): schema_search now returns signatures and its description says so. Runs started before this timestamp carried 2,159 B.

M-G2.note: One tool per frozen operation in services/operations/. src/test/operations.test.ts already fails if that set changes; this catches the other direction — Apollo MCP rendering the same operations into a different schema after a version bump.

M-G3.note: Apollo MCP Server with introspect disabled, so search is the only discovery tool — the condition asks whether targeted search alone is enough. Three tools like M-R2 (2,652 B) and the post-fix M-G1 (2,270 B), and at 1,940 B the smallest surface in the matrix. With introspect enabled it is 4 tools / 2,900 B, identical to phase-1 condition B; that is the number to expect if the config is ever flipped back. Measured with capture_mcp.py, whose len(json.dumps(tools)) uses default separators — a compact-separator measurement of the same surface reads 1,857 and is what this entry was first pinned at, wrongly.

M-R3.note: REST with no spec access at all: one tool, no openapi_search, no openapi_describe. At 786 B the smallest surface in the study — less than half M-G3's 1,940 B and a twelfth of M-R1's 9,601 B. The description is M-R2's rest_request minus one sentence, the pointer at the two discovery tools this mode does not expose (servers/openapi_mcp.py builds it from DISCOVERY_TOOLS at import so the two cannot drift, and raises if that sentence stops being present). What remains still names the three services, their resource families and two example paths, which is this condition's floor: a usable generic HTTP tool cannot say nothing. Fat bracket only — `?fields=` is documented in the spec and nowhere else, so an agent without the spec cannot learn it exists, and advertising it here would re-import the spec.
